I am 72 years old, and I have worked these fields for 50 years. My bones know the weather better than the television does. I have 14 mu: 9 mu will stay in my wheat-maize rotation, and 5 mu I will plant with cotton. I keep cotton because the buyer still comes to Quzhou, but at my age five mu is enough — any more and I could not finish the picking before the autumn rains come. My sons work in the county town, but they always return for wheat harvest and to help plant maize.

The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I ploughed deep then, and now I only need to manage it through the spring. I will irrigate three times from my well: at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I top-dress urea at green-up; that is usually enough nitrogen along with the autumn base. Two sprays — one for weeds and another if I see aphids. I use the improved seed from the county station, the same kind my neighbors use. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

When the wheat comes off in early June, I do not rest. I rotary till the stubble immediately and plant hybrid maize seed the same day — summer is short, and the maize must get its feet in the soil fast. I put fertilizer in the planting holes and side-dress later. Two irrigations should do, God willing, plus two sprays. Hybrid maize gives me about 600 kg per mu when it goes well.

For cotton, I plough the 5 mu in late March to break up the clods and let the sun warm the earth. I plant my improved cotton in late April — it has the Bt gene, so bollworm does not scare me as much as it used to. I irrigate three times and spray four times for aphids and mites. I do not over-fertilize; tall cotton is hard for an old man to pick. I expect 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. This is how I have done it for decades, and this is how I will do it this year.
